expected_effect: mongod is absent, not sick: SIGTERM at 10:07:18.971, clean teardown, exit 0, no startup line after. Recreating the container should yield fresh mongod startup lines in Loki for the mongodb-user pod ('Waiting for connections' on 27017) and then connection-accepted entries, within ~60s. Caller-side alerts against mongodb-user should clear.
if_wrong: No startup lines appear, or the pod logs another SIGTERM within minutes — meaning an external agent (the suspected failure-injection path) is still stopping these processes and the restart will be undone. Note mongodb-user emits no span metrics [tr_11db3f5b33a4], so confirmation must come from logs and caller alerts, not from its own error ratio.
risk: If the process is being re-killed by an active injector or a controller, the restart is a no-op that costs a pod recreate and masks the real actor. If the ConfigMap-driven admin/failure config is the cause, restarting re-applies it. Any in-flight writes at recreate are lost; mongod state is on disk but in-memory sessions and caches are discarded, and the recreate is not reversible.
blast_radius: One service. Every hotel-reservation caller of mongodb-user (user/auth path) sees connection resets for the recreate duration. Five sibling datastores remain down and unaddressed by this proposal.
